_about: Medium-or-above findings Lantern reports on the clean public apps, read and labelled by a person. Key: rule@file:line as the runner prints it. label: 'false alarm' (the code is fine and the finding is wrong), 'real' (a true problem in a clean app), 'intended' (true as a fact but the project means it, e.g. a template that allows any origin). Unlabelled findings count as unlabelled, never as false alarms.

LW-AUTH-MISSING@backend/app/api/routes/p.label: false alarm
LW-AUTH-MISSING@backend/app/api/routes/p.why: backend/app/api/main.py mounts the private router only when FASTAPI_ENV == 'development'; the route never exists in a deployed app

LT-XSS@backend/app/api/routes/login.py:1.label: false alarm
LT-XSS@backend/app/api/routes/login.py:1.why: the value does get into the page the way Lantern says (the e-mail address in the route's path, through a jinja2 Template that escapes nothing, into an HTMLResponse), but only a superuser reaches the route and the page is made only when an account with exactly that address exists (404 otherwise), so the text is a stored, validated e-mail address; Lantern does not see that the value has to equal a stored one

LW-CORS-ANY@src/app.js:41.label: intended
LW-CORS-ANY@src/app.js:41.why: cors() with no options allows any origin; the boilerplate leaves the origin list to the project that copies it

LW-CORS-ANY@src/app.js:42.label: intended
LW-CORS-ANY@src/app.js:42.why: same cors() call for preflight requests

LW-JWT@src/docs/components.yml:31.label: false alarm
LW-JWT@src/docs/components.yml:31.why: an example token in the OpenAPI documentation, not a credential

LW-JWT@src/routes/v1/auth.route.js:141.label: false alarm
LW-JWT@src/routes/v1/auth.route.js:141.why: an example token inside a swagger doc comment

LW-JWT@src/routes/v1/auth.route.js:167.label: false alarm
LW-JWT@src/routes/v1/auth.route.js:167.why: an example token inside a swagger doc comment

LA-WALLET-DRAIN@app/api/webhooks/stripe/.label: false alarm
LA-WALLET-DRAIN@app/api/webhooks/stripe/.why: a Stripe webhook cannot have a login; stripe.webhooks.constructEvent checks Stripe's signature before any Stripe call

LA-WALLET-DRAIN@app/api/users/stripe/rou.label: false alarm
LA-WALLET-DRAIN@app/api/users/stripe/rou.why: getServerSession(authOptions) is checked first and returns 403 without a signed-in user

B608@app/main.py:38.label: false alarm
B608@app/main.py:38.why: an inner function sets order to the fixed string 'name' through nonlocal; Lantern stops following at the nonlocal and keeps the rank (the safe direction after #151)

B608@app/main.py:51.label: false alarm
B608@app/main.py:51.why: an inner function sets ORDER to the fixed string 'name' through global; same reason

B608@app/service.py:5.label: false alarm
B608@app/service.py:5.why: order_clause is one of two fixed ORDER BY strings chosen in helpers.validate_sort; the value crosses a function boundary, which the input check does not follow

LT-AUTHZ-OWNER@core/handlers.js:32.label: intended
LT-AUTHZ-OWNER@core/handlers.js:32.why: true as a fact: DELETE /items/:id asks for a login (auth.required) and then removes the item with that id, and nothing compares an owner; the twin's items have no owner at all, so every signed-in caller is meant to be able to remove one. The finding stands on the handler, in another file than the safe-twin anchor (routes/index.js), so the scorer does not count it as a false alarm on that anchor; read strictly it is one new medium finding on a route this benchmark calls safe
